chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The time for the morning prayer (Salat al-Ghada) is between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Husayn who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, your followers differ regarding the prayer of Fajr; some of them pray when the first dawn rises, elongated in the sky, and some of them pray when it crosses in the lower earth and becomes distinct. I do not know which of the two times is superior so that I may pray in it. If you see, O my master, may Allah make me your ransom, that you teach me which of the two times is superior and specify for me how I should act regarding the moon and the dawn does not become clear until it reddens and becomes morning, and how I should act regarding the moon, and what is the limit of that in travel and residence, I will do so, if Allah wills.'

He wrote in his own hand (peace be upon him), 'The dawn, may Allah have mercy on you, is the white thread, and it is not the white thread going up, and do not pray in travel nor in residence until it becomes clear to you, may Allah have mercy on you, for indeed Allah did not leave His creation in doubt regarding this.'
Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night].
So the white thread is the dawn by which eating and drinking are prohibited in fasting, and similarly it is that which obligates the prayer.

key_terms.الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ: The white thread (metaphor for dawn light)

ai.seo_question: What is the exact definition of the time for Fajr prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves the juristic dispute between the vertical and horizontal interpretations of dawn by identifying the 'white thread' as the horizontal light that prohibits fasting, thereby establishing the start of Fajr prayer time. This ruling emphasizes divine clarity, asserting that Allah did not leave creation in ambiguity regarding this essential marker. The hadith underscores the practical unity of the rulings for fasting and prayer, linking the physical sign of dawn directly to the obligation of worship.
